description: We're a CSE student team from Dhaka building a browser-based web application : "Last Signal " for the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge . The main objective is to tell the story of fallen spacecrafts that once served for humanity form the view point of the Machine itself not by facts. Our team is fully formed and not currently seeking additional members, but we're excited to connect with fellow participants !
summary: Last Signal is a web app that gives a voice to NASA's retired spacecraft on the Moon and Mars, answering the challenge "Abandoned but not Forgotten". Readers find a spacecraft according to their mood by a short quiz or searching its name, and it tells its own first-person story, from launch to its final signal. Each story is built from NASA's official mission pages, NASA images and Wikipedia, and Google Gemini writes it using only those facts. A short quiz awards points and levels. It matters because these machines still hold real science and history, and Last Signal helps students and space fans remember them. The archive covers 12 spacecraft, including Spirit, Opportunity, Pioneer 10 and the Lunar Roving Vehicle.
details: What it does: Last Signal lets abandoned NASA spacecraft tell their own stories. A reader finds a spacecraft by answering a few yes/no questions or by searching a name. The app then gathers facts from our built-in archive, Wikipedia, NASA's official mission pages (NASA Science and NSSDCA) and NASA Image and Video Library pictures, and Google Gemini writes a first-person story in five parts: Launch, The Mission, The End, Where I Am Now, and The Science I Left Behind. Gemini is told to use only the supplied facts. A short quiz awards points, and the reader's level changes how the story is told. Benefits and impact: students and space fans learn the real history of spacecraft that finished their missions and still rest on the Moon and Mars, in a story they remember. It covers 12 spacecraft: Spirit, Opportunity, Sojourner, Ingenuity, Phoenix, InSight, Viking 1, Surveyor 3, the Lunar Roving Vehicle, ALSEP, Pioneer 10 and Kepler. Tools: Python and Flask, HTML and CSS, JavaScript, the Wikipedia REST API, the NASA Image and Video Library API, and the Google Gemini API. Creativity: spacecraft narrate their own endings, in a space-themed interface with a video background. Factors we considered: accuracy (the story only uses supplied facts, with a fallback to our built-in facts if a source is unavailable), source credit shown under every story, and simple access (the app needs only a name). Live app (free hosting, so the first load can be slow): https://last-signal-dcs6.onrender.com Next: connect more NASA datasets, add the remaining spacecraft from NASA's list, and host on our own website. SI disclosure: Google Gemini writes the stories at runtime. Claude AI helped with the UI redesign, the NASA page-reading . Some background and object images were created with AI tools.
